spec.title: PROP-044: Change-native formats — surviving perpetual evolution

status.comment: commissioned by the owner 2026-08-09 (mandate quoted in §1); synthesised from the schema-evolution discovery corpus, tree measurements, and a separately convened Fable verdict; RATIFIED by the owner 2026-08-13 («Ратификацию на сам PROP-044 даю») — the standing format ideology; the first build ran under the change-native campaign plan (executed whole and folded 2026-08-18) and the wave-2 TZ

p.PURPOSE: **What this document is.** The standing ideology for every durable data format this project reads or writes — package format, manifests, catalog, lockfile, configs, CLI JSON, MCP tool schemas. It is written to be handed to an AI agent as context: it states the laws, the machinery they require, the policy for each format, and the machine gates that make the laws enforceable against authors weaker than their reviewers. The first build that implemented it closed 2026-08-17, and what it decided now lives where it binds — the catalog's own contract [PROP-005](../modules/vibe-index/PROP-005-package-index.xml) and the docblocks of the generator layer under `xtask/src/codegen/`. The plan that carried that build was disposable by construction; this document is the contract.

mandate.title: 1. The environment, in the owner's words

p.MANDATE-VERBATIM: **The owner's mandate (2026-08-09, verbatim, the frame every rule below serves):** «Совершенно все пакеты будут в ближайшем будущем опубликованы наружу на миллионы людей. И эволюция будет максимально быстрая — мы ещё 10 раз сменим формат и манифеста, и пакетов, и чего угодно. И да, у людей всё будет ломаться и им придётся перекачивать. Разрушения БУДУТ — это неотъемлемая часть идеи move fast and break things. Ты не можешь выпускать по 10 версий продукта в день (реально 10!) и ничего не сломать. Через год вообще всё будет другое. Нам нужна система, которая переживает такой процесс. Maven, RPM и так далее — они не про это, они рассчитаны на стабильность. У нас нет и не будет никогда никакой настоящей стабильности, хотя очень круто иметь хотя бы ПЕРИОДЫ СТАБИЛЬНОСТИ. Все обязательства типа "никогда не переименовывать" будут держаться ровно до тех пор, пока мы их не нарушим — а однажды мы их точно нарушим, ЛЮБОЕ из обязательств. Эта система должна воспринимать рефакторинги как нормальную часть жизни, а не как редкое катастрофическое событие.»

p.THE-INVERSION: **The inversion this forces.** Stability-era ecosystems minimise the *frequency* of breaking change — they make a break so expensive it almost never happens (additive-only forever, never rename, five-year windows). A change-native system minimises the *cost* of each break: detection, migration and recovery are cheap, routine, and rehearsed. The machinery budget moves from prevention to recovery. Every technique borrowed from the stability world must be re-derived under this inversion or discarded; several invert outright.

p.TWO-CLOCKS: **Product clocks and wire clocks are different clocks.** Ten product releases a day is the product clock. The wire — bytes a foreign parser reads — changes only by the deliberate acts this document regulates. The whole point of the machinery below is that a wire change can never again be a *side effect* of a refactoring: it is always a named, gated, recorded act. That separation, not slowness, is what makes ten releases a day survivable.

laws.title: 2. The two laws, and the short list of the forbidden

p.LAW-NO-LYING: **Law 1 — break freely; never lie.** A break that announces itself — a parse refusal with a recipe, a skipped record with a reason, a tombstone — is normal life; users re-fetch and continue. Forbidden is the family of changes where a *wrong answer looks like a right one*: silent misinterpretation is the single failure mode that re-downloading cannot cure, because the error propagates into derived state before anyone knows.

p.LAW-NO-UNRECOVERABLE: **Law 2 — delete freely; never make state unrecoverable.** Every published artifact must be reconstructible, byte for byte, from the authoritative core (§3). A fact that would be lost by deleting a derived artifact is a secretly-authoritative fact, and it is promoted into the journal the moment it is found. This law is what *purchases* the freedom to break: we may discard any format because nothing of record lives in it.

p.forbidden-lead: From these two laws, the complete list of the absolutely forbidden — note how short it is, and note what is NOT on it (renaming, deleting, narrowing, restructuring are all permitted):

facts.FORBID-IDENTIFIER-REUSE: Never reuse an identifier — a field name, a vocabulary value, a `name@version` coordinate — with a changed meaning and no declaration. Old data would parse successfully and be understood wrongly: the one unfixable failure. (For coordinates this is already standing law: `spec://org.vibevm.world/qualified-naming/flows/qualified-naming/QUALIFIED-NAMING-PROTOCOL#root`.)
facts.FORBID-BYTE-MUTATION: Never change bytes at an existing address — and an "address" is a **frozen** coordinate: a version whose manifest carries `frozen = true`, plus any content-hash-named object. Republishing a frozen version with different content is the break a correct client cannot even detect; it silently poisons every hash, cache and lockfile downstream. An *unfrozen* version is not an address but a **snapshot** (§2a), and its content flowing is normal life, not a violation.
facts.FORBID-SILENCE: Never answer silence for a name that ever existed. Every once-valid name resolves to the current thing, a forwarding pointer, or a tombstone with a reason. Silence is indistinguishable from network failure; it converts a clean break into a riddle, and riddles — not breaks — are what actually strand users.
facts.FORBID-SECRET-TRUTH: Never create unrecoverable state: an authoritative fact living only in a derived artifact, or an unreproducible build. This forfeits the right to delete-and-rebuild, i.e. the foundation of every other freedom here.
facts.FORBID-HANDWRITTEN-WIRE: Never hand-write a parser or writer for one of our own wire formats inside this tree. Not a goal in itself: it is the mechanism by which the first four violations happen unnoticed.

p.THE-FREEZE-MODEL: **2a. Frozen and snapshot versions (owner rulings, 2026-08-10; terminology fixed 2026-08-13).** A version is a **snapshot by default** — the word carries its Maven sense, *mutable*: content may change under the same version string, `vibe update` brings the fresh content without regard for hash continuity, and the lockfile pins the delivered capture's `content_hash` plus an opaque provider locator for reproduction. The **freeze** is the package author's one-way act: `frozen = true` in the manifest — never a registry's opinion, never part of the version string. The carrier decisions and their reasons: *(i)* the flag lives **inside the hashed content**, so a frozen version self-describes even offline and every registry serving those bytes necessarily agrees — in a multi-registry world with no global journal, content is the only carrier that cannot diverge; registries merely *observe* a freeze in their journals and project it into catalogs; *(ii)* the version string carries version ordering **only** — two entities never share one name, which keeps the full matrix expressible: a frozen prerelease (an immutable published beta) and a mutable bare version (being stabilised in place) are both legal; *(iii)* the transition is **one-way and single** — unfreezing is forbidden, further work is a new version string; a registry may never accept a frozen coordinate's re-publication with different bytes; *(iv)* same coordinate + different bytes + any party claiming frozen = **loud conflict** through the candidate machinery, never a quiet pick. **Every surface that shows a version shows its frozen state** — machine outputs carry the field by schema; CLI, TUI, GUI and MCP render it always (the Maven lesson: mutability a human cannot see is mutability that will surprise them). Yank remains journal-borne — it is the act frozen content can no longer carry itself.

p.TERMS-SNAPSHOT-FROZEN-CHANNEL: **2b. The terminology, fixed explicitly (owner ruling, 2026-08-13) — one boolean axis, three words, no synonyms.** **snapshot** ≡ `frozen = false` (the default: content may flow under the version string; a hash mismatch is *news*) and **frozen** ≡ `frozen = true` (the one-way author act: bytes immutable; a hash mismatch is an *alarm*) are **antonyms — the two states of the one `frozen` axis, with no third state.** The word **channel** belongs exclusively to the *other* axis: an author-named version pointer (`stable`, `beta`, … — [PROP-005 §2.18](../modules/vibe-index/PROP-005-package-index.xml#channels)); a channel may point at a snapshot or at a frozen version — the axes are orthogonal, and «замороженная бета» stays expressible. A storage provider's immutable point-in-time object is a **capture** and its mutable named pointer a **named ref** (`##PROVIDER-NEUTRALITY`) — never "snapshot", never "channel". The one pre-existing distinct sense — `materialization = "snapshot"` (PROP-022 §2.2, the vendored-copy mode) — was flagged rather than silently changed, and the owner renamed it the same day: the mode is **`copy`**, so `snapshot` now carries exactly one sense in the system.

laws.p: The scoped [Redbook composition policy](PROP-000.xml#REDBOOK-COMPOSITION-POLICY) permits mutable tested-roster updates within the owner-selected next 1.1.0 line without another increment or version question. Preserve the delivered Developer Preview 1 boundary; edition labels do not replace exact delivered content identity. Retained captures and content-hash objects remain immutable; this policy does not authorize rewriting frozen foreign coordinates, historical Git objects or evidence. Generic non-Redbook freeze rules remain unchanged. Public distribution of 1.1.0 is prohibited until the later explicit grant required by [NEXT-PUBLICATION-HOLD](PROP-000.xml#NEXT-PUBLICATION-HOLD).

p.TRUTH-KERNEL: **The authoritative core is small, and everything else is disposable.** Authoritative: (1) package sources at immutable git commits; (2) the authored `vibe.toml` inside those commits; (3) the **registry facts journal** — append-only records of what sources cannot carry: publication, yank, rename, removal, ownership, security notice; (4) the schemas, hash recipes and the generator in this repository — the contract *is* source code; (5) the format registry and break notes — the ledger of what we broke.

p.THE-JOURNAL-STAYS-APPEND-ONLY-AND-THAT-H: **Decision (owner, 2026-08-19): the journal is append-only, it is not truncated, and the reach of that rule is stated here rather than discovered.** Because every publication is a permanent record, **a name published once is named in the journal for good** — removing a package from the catalog, and even deleting its source repository, does not unname it there. The catalog is a projection and can be rebuilt without the name; the journal cannot be edited to forget it.

p.JOURNAL-REDACTION-IS-A-SEPARATE-MECHANIS: **Deliberately not built, and named so it is not mistaken for an oversight.** An operator may one day need a removal that reaches the journal itself — the mechanism is theirs to invoke and this project does not ask what for. No current plan contains it, nothing in the tree approximates it, and no existing verb is to be widened into it: a facility that can edit the truth layer must be its own deliberate operation, because the property every other rule here leans on is that the journal is the one thing nothing rewrites. *Revisit when:* an operator states a need that catalog-side removal cannot satisfy.

p.DERIVED-IS-DISPOSABLE: **Derived and deletable at any moment:** the entire catalog (every wire type it serves), `vibe.lock`, caches, generated types, clients, validators and docs, published projections, CLI JSON outputs, all aggregates (`latest_stable`, counters, sizes), and `content_hash` values — derived, but stamped with their recipe (§4.7).

p.MANIFEST-IS-THE-CENTRE: **How this squares with "we manage packages that have manifests": the manifest is the centre of this architecture, not a casualty of it.** "Disposable worlds" never refers to packages — package content at a tag is immutable truth, and a lockfile pinned to a `content_hash` reproduces an install across any number of catalog rebuilds. What is disposable is every *serving form* of the metadata. The manifest leads a double life, and the split is the design: as an **authored file in the package repo** it is part of the authoritative kernel — the contract between the author and vibe, strict, epoch-marked, migrated by codemod; as **data consumed at scale** it is never served raw — the indexer (the one place holding the wide multi-epoch reading window) reads it at the tagged ref and projects it into the current-epoch catalog and the published projection. So when the manifest format changes for the tenth time, no published package is re-authored: its old-epoch manifest stays readable by one frozen reader in one codebase, and its *entry* is simply re-projected. The system manages manifest-bearing packages precisely by refusing to let the hand-written manifest double as the wire format for millions.

p.MEMBERSHIP-IS-TESTED: **Membership in "derived" is machine-tested, not argued:** delete the artifact, rebuild it from a pinned input snapshot, compare bytes (`rebuild --check`). A difference means a secret truth was found, and its home is the journal. This one test closes an entire class of architecture drift, which is why it is built early, not last.

p.PROVIDER-NEUTRALITY: **Storage-provider neutrality (owner ruling, 2026-08-10): git is a representation, never the semantics.** Repositories may live outside git, so the system's meaning binds only to **provider obligations**, of which git is implementation №1: *(i)* serve an immutable capture for a durable reference, *(ii)* serve a mutable named ref and answer "what capture is behind it now", *(iii)* answer a cheap freshness question about a named ref, *(iv)* enumerate an organisation. How a provider honours them is its own business — the git provider uses tags, branches, commits and history; an object store would use versioned objects and retention; an OCI registry, digests. Three consequences bind every design in this document: **the authoritative act is always a journal event, never a storage operation** (a tag is how the git provider *implements* a freeze-like obligation, not what the freeze *is*); **the universal verifier is our own `content_hash`**, computed over file bytes and already provider-neutral — the system never trusted a provider's reference semantics, it verifies content, so a provider that lies is caught by the same check everywhere; and **wire fields that locate content at a provider (`source_ref`, `resolved_commit` and kin) are opaque locator strings owned by the provider named in the URL — no reader interprets their internal shape.** Wherever this document says "git" ("free because the transport is git", "raw files in git"), read it as the git provider's way of meeting an obligation — the durability of frozen worlds is an obligation every provider must meet, which git happens to get free from history immutability.

p.ONE-ETERNAL-FILE: **Exactly one file is eternal: the handshake.** A tiny document — `{vibe, worlds[], min_client, notice, successor}` — through which a client of any age learns which worlds currently exist, where they live, what to do when it understands none of them, and where the handshake itself moved (`successor` is the in-band forwarding pointer; our transport is raw files in git, so there are no HTTP redirects to lean on). Its keys never change meaning. Everything else in the system is disposable precisely because this one thing is not. This is the system's single eternal vow, and it is priced deliberately: five keys and a pointer.

p.MACHINERY-LEAD: Compatibility here is a property of machinery around formats, never of formats themselves. The machinery, each piece multiplying the others:

p.M-FORMAT-REGISTRY: **4.1 The format registry.** `formats/REGISTRY.toml` inventories every surface a foreign parser reads: id, epoch, schema path, recoverable-or-not, independent-parser count, sunset date, golden-corpus path. From it the `FormatId` enum is generated, and all wire I/O goes through `wire::publish(FormatId, …)` / `wire::load(FormatId, …)` — an unregistered format is *inexpressible in the type system*, not merely discouraged. An unnumbered format is a format that will be broken without anyone noticing.

p.M-SCHEMA-DESCRIBES-FORM: **4.2 Schemas describe form; the generator owns policy.** One schema per format per epoch (`schemas/<format>/e<N>/…`). The schema language (JTD today) is chosen for *poverty*, not power: an agent cannot write a half-tagged union or a conditional schema in it. Everything the language cannot express — strictness, open vocabularies with preserved unknown values, skip-empty conventions, canonical ordering, determinism — is emitted by **our own generator layer**, which is a first-class component of this project. A third-party generator's expressiveness never decides our policy. Measured 2026-08-09: stock `jtd-codegen 0.4.1` handles tagged unions (`#[serde(tag)]`) but emits closed vocabularies and `Option<Box<…>>` optionals — exactly the gap the layer exists to close.

p.M-WIRE-FIELD-ORDER: **Exact object-member byte order is opt-in and schema-declared.** JTD property-map order has no meaning and is never inferred. A root or named-definition object that requires a stable serialization order carries `metadata."x-wire-order"`: one array containing every required and optional wire member exactly once. The generator validates that complete census, resolves each member through the generated Rust field's surviving serde rename or snake-case identity, and moves the complete final field chunk before strictness and domain renaming. Missing, duplicate, unknown, non-string or non-object annotations and unfamiliar generator shapes refuse generation. Without the key the pass is byte-identical.

p.M-OPEN-ENUM-FROM-CLOSED: **4.2a The vocabulary resolution.** From a *closed* schema enum the generator emits an *open* Rust type: `enum { …known…, Unknown(String) }`. Compiler-checked exhaustiveness survives (the `Unknown` arm is mandatory), the original string is preserved through any rewrite, and tolerance of future values is structural. The trilemma the discovery corpus recorded — tagging vs fallback values vs codegen, mutually incompatible — dissolves because the decision moved from the schema language into the generator.

p.M-WIDE-INTEGERS-AS-STRINGS: **4.2b Integers wider than 32 bits ride the wire as decimal strings** *(owner ruling 2026-08-20, the B-091 fork answered once and generally)*. JTD (RFC 8927) has no 64-bit integer type at all — the pinned generator rejects `uint64` and `int64` as InvalidType (measured 2026-08-15) — so every field wider than 32 bits would otherwise re-litigate the same bad trilemma: a `uint32` that is false at and above 2³², a `float64` that loses precision past 2⁵³, or an untyped `{}` that loses the field entirely. The general answer: such a field is encoded as a **canonical decimal string** — ASCII digits only, no sign, no leading zeros except `"0"` itself — the schema says `string`, the Rust type stays the true integer, conversion lives at the serde boundary, and non-canonical input is refused loudly rather than coerced. Timestamps are not this rule's business: they ride as RFC 3339 through the `timestamp` vocabulary. First application: the catalog manifest's file `size` (`formats/breaks/003.md`).

p.WIDE-INTEGERS-CLASS-BOUNDARY: **The class boundary is domain honesty, not the Rust type** *(ADR-part; owner accepted the recommendation 2026-08-20, closing BACKLOG B-095)*. The one question asked of a field: does its DOMAIN honestly fit `uint32`? A count bounded by construction (a page size capped in code, a result count bounded by the corpus) says `uint32` in the schema and crosses the boundary through a **checked** conversion — never a silent `as` — failing loudly on the unreachable overflow. A field whose domain does not fit (a lifetime request counter, an uptime) is this rule's subject and rides as the canonical decimal string, because a `uint32` schema would lie on a long-lived server and a JSON number breaks silently past 2⁵³ — the exact silent-drift genre this document exists to kill. There is no third category and no exception list: alternatives weighed were per-field exceptions (each invites the next negotiation) and float64 numbers (honest until they are not). Applied 2026-08-20 across both envelope families: three admin counters became strings, twenty-two count-class fields became checked `uint32`, and their recorded schema deviations died.

p.M-CANONICAL-BYTES: **4.3 Canonical bytes, deterministic writers.** One state — one byte sequence: sorted keys, injected clocks (a writer never calls `now()`; time arrives as input), pinned encodings, deterministic compression. Determinism is not cosmetics; it is the *measuring instrument*: it makes "rebuild and compare" a real verification, an empty diff a real no-op, and a wire-diff a quantitative measure of any break.

p.M-JOURNAL-NOT-RMW: **4.4 Journal and projection — no read-modify-write.** Mutations of derived artifacts are appends to the journal followed by reprojection; a writer never accepts as input a value parsed from its own published output (machine-enforced at module boundaries). This dissolves the worst hazard the discovery found — "tolerant reading without capture silently deletes foreign fields on the next rewrite" — not by adding capture machinery but by removing the rewrite: there is nothing to preserve because nothing read is ever written back. Reader strictness can then be dropped for free.

p.M-MUST-UNDERSTAND: **4.5 must-understand and record quarantine.** Each record names the capabilities a reader must have to act on it. A reader lacking them quarantines *that record* — the file loads, the server starts, and the refusal surfaces at the point of use with a generated recipe ("unavailable because X; run Y"). This is the exact inversion of additive-only: there the *schema* promises ignorability forever; here the *writer* declares it per record, addressably and revocably. Unknown fields outside must-understand are ignored; unknown records are quarantined, never dropped silently.

p.M-EPOCHS: **4.6 Epochs are parallel worlds, not mutations.** A heavy break mints a new epoch at a new path (`/e4/…`); the old world keeps publishing until its announced sunset, then freezes — free of charge, because the transport is git. Worlds are physically unable to poison each other. Within an epoch, obligations hold; epoch boundaries are where "we will one day break any vow" happens in a controlled, rehearsed, announced way. Light breaks (a new capability under must-understand) need no epoch at all.

p.M-BREAK-WINDOW: **4.7 Breaking is a switched resource; recipes are data.** `formats/EPOCHS.toml` carries `break_window_open`; while it is closed, CI refuses any change under `schemas/**` or `formats/**` — a *period of stability* is the state of a flag, visible in the git log of one file, not a virtue or a hope. Any wire-visible change requires a break note (`formats/breaks/NNN.md`: what · epoch · who fixes · sunset · user recipe), and the golden-corpus wire-diff must be empty or covered by one — the gate does not forbid breaks, it makes an *unannounced* break impossible. Every derived value carries its recipe id (`content_hash` rides as `sha256-tree/1:…`, the exclusion list and normalisation live in `hash_recipes/1.toml` as data, each recipe frozen by a golden test) — changing a computation becomes a visible new recipe, never a silent change of every value in the world.

p.PLACEMENT-LADDER: **The placement ladder.** Cost of change grows monotonically: config < lockfile < index export files < `by-name` projection < journal < `vibe.toml` < identity/handshake. The one placement rule a weak author can apply without understanding the system: **put every new fact on the lowest rung that bears it.** A volatile fact in the manifest is a decade-long debt; the same fact in the lockfile is free.

p.POLICY-IS-COMPUTED: **A format's policy is computed, not chosen**, from two axes: is it recoverable without a human, and how many independent parsers exist. Recoverable + one parser → hard gate + silent rebuild (lockfile, caches). Recoverable + many parsers → epochs, parallel publication, generated clients, narrow projection (catalog, CLI JSON). Unrecoverable + one parser → epoch-in-file + codemod (configs). Unrecoverable + many parsers is the worst quadrant — minimise it, epoch it, migrate it by bot (`vibe.toml` is the only resident, and creating a *new* format in this quadrant requires an explicit owner decision recorded in the format registry).

p.MIGRATION-TAXONOMY: **Migrations come in three kinds, and two must not exist.** Derived data has *no migrations ever* — delete and rebuild; writing an index migrator is an architecture error, because it asserts the index is authoritative. Authored data gets *codemods*: idempotent, comment-preserving (document-edit in place, never serialise-from-struct), rehearsed on a corpus of real files, applied locally by `vibe migrate` and remotely by bot pull request — the one scalable way to migrate data you do not own, and a capability a git-organisation registry has that Maven Central structurally lacks. Runtime compatibility shims are forbidden; the only exception is frozen per-epoch *readers* of old manifests inside the indexer — readers, not shims: they branch no logic and are never edited after freezing.

p.MIGRATION-PLAN-LAW:
**Pure authored-manifest migration planning.** A planner consumes exact in-memory source text and explicitly selected source profile, target profile and recipe. A missing selection produces typed input requirements with named alternatives; an unknown profile or revision, incompatible edge, malformed syntax or unrecognized shape produces a typed refusal. Neither the package's product version nor an absent epoch selects a grammar. Absence remains the distinct pre-epoch state; a recipe never inserts an epoch or changes an unrelated authored selection as a convenience.
Recognized grammars are finite, immutable named revisions, checked over the owning TOML syntax tree. Their exact field sets, primitive shapes and value vocabularies are frozen independently of the evolving current Manifest decoder. A new shape needs a new profile revision. The initial bounded recipe is the documented materialization `snapshot` to `copy` rename, rehearsed on retained historical fixture bytes with immutable provenance. A retained test fixture proves its recognized case, not a real-file corpus; that broader rehearsal remains required before claiming broad migration support. This recipe does not implement the complete historical manifest language. Current pre-epoch and explicit epoch-1 identity profiles remain distinct. SourceDescriptor, feature-specific converters and effectful application are separate atoms.
The first registry entries are `materialization-legacy-absent-r1`, `materialization-current-absent-r1` and `materialization-current-epoch1-r1`. Their bounded package-role grammar admits only root `package` and optional `requires`; package requires string `name`, `group`, `kind`, `version`, with kind in `flow`, `feat`, `stack`, `tool`, `mcp`, `lang`. Optional strings are `materialization`, `license`, `description`, `homepage`; optional string arrays are `authors`, `keywords`; optional booleans are `bridge`, `frozen`. Epoch is absent in the two absent profiles and integer 1 in the epoch-1 profile. Requires admits only `packages`, whose owner-qualified keys map to string constraints or tables with required string `version` and optional string `link`, one of `static`, `dynamic`, `static-transitive`, `static-hard`. The frozen structural key shape is `[kind:]group/name`: exactly one slash, nonempty group and name, no `@`, and at most one optional colon prefix whose kind is in the six-token package vocabulary above. The current naming owner still checks group/name and constraint semantics; it cannot remove this structural qualification requirement from a frozen profile. Normal and inline TOML tables are equivalent shapes. Every other key, shape or vocabulary is refused. Legacy materialization is required and exactly `snapshot`; current materialization is absent or `copy`, `hardlink`, `in-place`. The only nonidentity edge is `snapshot-to-copy-r1`, from legacy absent to current absent; `identity-r1` covers the two current profiles each to itself. No edge adds an epoch. Current semantic validation may refuse an otherwise recognized shape; that never widens this frozen grammar.
A successful plan carries exact before and after text, ordered token edits, source/target/recipe identities, deterministic domain-framed content and diff identities, and an output checked by the current Manifest owner. That final checker validates the result; it does not define the frozen input grammar. All bytes outside selected token spans, including comments, order, quote style and owner values, survive unchanged. An unprovable edit refuses instead of serializing a struct or falling back. Identity plans are byte-identical with no edits. Repeating exact input and selection reproduces exact output and identities. Planning performs no filesystem, cache, lock, provider, LLM, publication or implicit application operation.
The initial identity recipe uses SHA-256 and frames each byte string with its unsigned 64-bit big-endian byte length. Content frames the UTF-8 domain `vibe-manifest-content-r1` then the exact document bytes. Diff frames `vibe-manifest-migration-diff-r1`, source profile, target profile, recipe, before text and after text, then the edit count encoded as an unsigned 64-bit big-endian value inside a frame. Each edit in source order frames field path, original byte start and end (each encoded likewise), before token and after token. Digests are lowercase hexadecimal without a prefix. A fixed independently computed golden vector binds this recipe; changing domains, framing or ordering requires a distinct recipe revision.

p.MIGRATION-TRANSPORT-LAW:
**One pure domain owner, strict generated transports.** Register `migration-plan-request`, `migration-plan-report` and `migration-plan-error` at wire epoch 1, under `schemas/migration/e1/`, with explicit `unknown_fields = "deny"`. Product 1.1.0, the authored manifest epoch and these wire epochs remain independent. A request has `schema = 1`, exact `source_text` and optional string selections `source_profile`, `target_profile` and `recipe`. Missing selections reach the domain's typed questions; an unrecognized string reaches its typed refusal. Wrong primitive types, unknown fields or unsupported request schema fail preflight without calling the planner. There are no path, provider, apply, project or authority fields. Optional selections are omittable, not nullable: explicit JSON null is a preflight type error, not an unsupplied choice. The owning request decoder checks that presence distinction before lowering into optional Rust fields; it uses the existing JSON value/derived-reader path, not another parser or a generic schema interpreter.
A report has `schema = 1`, stage `planner`, and a discriminated outcome: `planned`, `no_op`, `needs_input` or `refused`. Planned and no-op outcomes carry selected profiles/recipe, exact before/after text, ordered byte-span token edits and the three existing identities. Wire edit offsets are canonical unsigned decimal strings: ASCII digits, no leading zero except `0`, checked against the original UTF-8 byte bounds. JTD has no uint64; an offset is never narrowed to uint32 or carried through a lossy float. Their source and target epoch markers are explicit `absent` or `epoch_1` discriminators with empty payloads, derived from the selected frozen profiles by the core owner; absent is never numeric zero or an inferred epoch 1. Questions carry their selected field and named choices. Refusal carries a typed error. No checked Manifest struct is serialized into this transport, and no unobserved epoch is invented for questions or refusals.
The standalone error document has `schema = 1`, stage `preflight` and a typed error; it is distinct from a planner-entered refusal. One shared JTD error fragment owns closed codes `invalid_request`, `unsupported_schema`, `input_read`, `unknown_selection`, `incompatible_edge`, `malformed_syntax`, `unrecognized_shape`, `invalid_current_manifest`, `unprovable_edit`, plus field and fixed reason strings. Preflight uses the first three codes; domain refusal uses the last six. Generated readers and the owning presence check enforce structural shape; the pure adapter checks schema/stage/code and result invariants before emission. The common error object is shared through the existing vocabulary resolver, not a primitive alias pretending to be an object or a second error codec. All nested payloads, empty epoch markers and the shared error reject unknown fields. Shared and consumer generation use the registry's effective `unknown_fields` policy; parser population cannot override explicit deny. Only an absent policy takes the loader's legacy default; an explicitly present non-string or unknown policy is a typed authoring refusal. Conflicting shared reader policies refuse rather than emitting divergent types or choosing the first consumer.
CLI `vibe refactor plan-migration` consumes JSON stdin by default or the explicit `--request-json` string, then emits exactly one registered report or error document. Its entry runs before configuration promotion, tracing, context, registry and other state initialization. Planned/no-op exit 0; input-required and invalid request/schema exit 2; domain refusal and stdin failure exit 1. The existing exit taxonomy is reused. MCP tool `plan_manifest_migration` invokes the same pure adapter and does not inspect ServerContext. Planner results survive in structuredContent; missing choices are a nonerror question report, domain refusal is a structured tool error, and malformed transport retains a typed preflight report through the ToolError channel without pretending the planner ran. No tool-name logic belongs in the dispatcher.
Exact text and authored diagnostic keys are caller-supplied data deliberately carried in this response; parser diagnostics and external/private context are not added. One-shot planning creates no files, cache, lock or provider work. CLI/MCP parity, actual isolated startup, strict nested decoder failures and selected profile/epoch/identity preservation must be verified on these surfaces; the final facade, mutation/apply, broad historical corpus and public publication remain separate obligations.

p.MIGRATION-APPLY-LAW:
**Portable application with declared guarantees.** Applying a validated manifest migration is an explicit effectful operation, separate from pure planning. Linux, macOS and Windows each require a usable implementation. Missing unrestricted content-CAS alone does not disable a platform. The initial portable contract serializes participating migration clients through a common project barrier, revalidates the selected frozen profiles, epochs, recipe and exact approved source bytes under that barrier, and publishes the validated after bytes. The existing planner owns the text transformation and its domain-framed identities; filesystem snapshots retain their separate raw byte identity recipe. A caller cannot supply an unchecked after document.
The barrier scope is explicit. Advisory locks and comparison followed by rename do not provide unconditional content-CAS against processes that ignore the protocol, including previously opened writable handles or mappings. An external writer can race the final comparison and publication. A matching observation does not prove that no intervening edit occurred. Document these limits, expose the achieved concurrency and durability guarantees in the registered result, and emit typed actionable warnings when an operation observes conflict, uncertain publication, reduced durability or unresolved residue. Do not promise detection of every uncooperating race. Participation by editor buffers is a later adapter obligation, not an implicit prerequisite or an already implemented exclusion mechanism.
Before any target mutation, durably retain exact approved before bytes and relevant preservation metadata, the validated plan, bounded target authority and operation intent in an explicitly selected recovery store. The store is physically disjoint from the target; publication stages stay on the target filesystem when required by the owning primitive. Retained approved images are distinct from mutable or potentially foreign project entries. Planning, a path spelling, package version 1.1.0 and a journal identifier alone grant no authority to update a path. The authorized operation is limited to its selected owned authored file; frozen published coordinates, historical captures, fixtures and upstream data are not inferred write targets.
Journal each durable boundary so interruption immediately before or after any write can be inspected after process exit. Reports distinguish completed, pending and uncertain effects; an error is not evidence of no mutation. Observation of approved before bytes, validated after bytes, absence and an unknown third state have distinct meanings. Recovery revalidates its retained intent and actual target state under the same participating-client barrier. An exact completed replay is idempotent. Recovery may complete or restore only a supported, proved prefix; it preserves unknown occupants and retained residue, refuses ambiguous automatic action, and reports what remains. Successful rollback is claimed only after its resulting state is verified. Do not silently overwrite a detected third state or discard the sole retained source image while recovering.
Actual platform and filesystem primitives own namespace anchoring, no-follow checks, publication and synchronization. Describe achieved durability and uncertain effects honestly when a primitive cannot confirm them. A genuine filesystem, authority or synchronization failure may refuse with its precise reason; it is not a blanket operating-system exclusion. Implemented platform paths and native-platform test evidence are separate claims. Verify the bounded migration's preservation, approved-byte conflict checks, repeat behavior and each interruption boundary; measure actual native platform behavior before claiming that platform's proof complete. Product version, authored format epoch, wire epoch and journal protocol revision remain independent.

MANIFEST-MIGRATION-APPLICATION-WIRE.title: Bounded application wire and journal protocol

p.MIGRATION-APPLICATION-WIRE-LAW:
**One bounded migration protocol.** Register generated strict formats `migration-operation-request`, `migration-operation-report` and `migration-application-journal` at wire epoch 1 under `schemas/migration/e1/`. All use `unknown_fields = deny`. Request/report are recoverable projections; the retained application journal is authoritative recovery state, not derived data. Product 1.1.0, manifest epoch, wire epoch and journal protocol revision remain distinct. This protocol covers one owned authored file and adds no universal operation engine.
The request root has integer `schema = 1` and discriminator `operation` with `apply`, `inspect`, `recover`. Every branch carries `operation_id` and `authority`: explicit absolute `project_root` and `recovery_store_root`, portable project-relative `target_relative`, and singleton `scope` `owned_authored_file`. These declarations require the admitting caller's bounded write authority; they are not filesystem ownership evidence. Apply also carries `approved_request_json` and `before_content_id`, `after_content_id`, `diff_id`. The JSON string is decoded by the existing strict pure-planning request owner, including its null-presence checks, then replayed by the planner. All three identities must match a planned/no-op result. No caller-supplied unchecked after document or duplicate planning payload codec is introduced. Recover carries `expected_intent_id` and explicit `action` `complete` or `restore`; inspect introduces no new durable intent.
All clients for a physical project root use its existing safefs opaque identity token as their project-lock key in the same explicitly designated physical recovery store. Store identity has its own opaque identity-token domain. Different stores and ancestor/descendant project scopes are outside this common-barrier guarantee; document that limit. Inspection opens only existing store/lock state and creates no files or directories. Apply may initialize its selected store. Relative operands remain capability anchored, no-follow, regular and single-link under the existing filesystem owner.
The journal has `schema = 1`, `protocol_revision = 1`, `operation_id`, `intent_id`, `authority`, `project_binding`, `store_binding`, `approved_request_json`, the three planner identities, `before_raw_sha256`, `after_raw_sha256`, canonical unsigned decimal string `before_length` and `after_length`, nullable uint32 `unix_mode`, and phase `prepared`, `publishing`, `published`, `restoring` or `restored`. Exact before bytes are retained separately as `before.bin`; prepared intent becomes durable only after that image is verified. Journal updates replace a whole strictly validated checkpoint; no append parser is added. Immutable intent fields must match on every replay. File bytes and Unix permission mode are the initial preservation scope; do not imply preservation of ACLs, extended attributes, ownership or timestamps. Report the actual narrower scope.
Identity recipes use SHA-256 with unsigned 64-bit big-endian byte-length framing, as the existing planner does. The operation storage key frames `vibe-manifest-migration-operation-r1`, physical project binding and operation id, in that order. Its lowercase hex digest names `migrations/{key}/before.bin` and `migrations/{key}/journal.json` below the selected store. The intent identity frames `vibe-manifest-migration-intent-r1`, operation id, physical project/store bindings, authority project/store spellings, target-relative path, scope, approved request JSON, before/after/diff content identities, raw before/after SHA-256 strings, before/after decimal lengths, and mode (`absent` or canonical unsigned decimal), in that order. Phase is excluded. Planner content hashes and raw filesystem hashes remain separate fields and recipes. Apply/restore stages use the existing `.vibe-stage-tx-` grammar with the first 32 lowercase hex digits of a SHA-256 digest framing `vibe-manifest-migration-stage-r1`, intent identity and `apply` or `restore`. A stage spelling alone never proves ownership.
Before publication checkpoint `publishing`; after verified publication checkpoint `published`. Restore similarly brackets its write with `restoring` and verified `restored`. Reinspect actual bytes after every possibly published error or interruption. Automatic completion supports an exact approved-before state; automatic restoration supports an exact validated-after state. Absent, unknown third or unreadable states require explicit resolution and preserve retained evidence. A matching completed replay makes no new target write; a restored terminal operation is not silently reapplied. Interrupted before-image preparation without valid intent may leave inspectable residue but grants no target mutation or automatic cleanup.
The report has integer `schema = 1`, required nullable `operation` and `operation_id` (null when malformed input supplies no valid identity), and outcome `completed`, `no_op`, `pending`, `uncertain`, `refused`; `target_state` is `approved_before`, `validated_after`, `absent`, `third_state`, `unavailable`. It carries required nullable intent/before/after/diff identities and a required nullable typed error, plus arrays `effects`, `warnings`, `residue`. Each effect has kind `store_bootstrap`, `barrier`, `before_image`, `journal`, `target_publication`, `target_restore` and state `not_started`, `completed`, `pending`, `uncertain`. Residue rows have location `store` or `project`, relative path and ownership `proved` or `unproven`; reporting a row grants no removal authority.
`guarantees` carries platform `linux`, `macos`, `windows`, `other`, concurrency `participating_clients` or `unestablished`, required nullable `barrier_binding`, boolean `uncooperating_writers_excluded` (always false in this protocol), durability `file_and_directory_synced`, `journal_recoverable`, `unconfirmed`, and preservation `bytes_and_unix_mode` or `bytes_only`. The aggregate never exceeds the weakest observed boundary; preflight and uncertain synchronization must not fabricate an achieved guarantee. Required nullable report fields explicitly carry null for unavailable evidence; omission is a structural refusal, unlike the nonnullable optional choices of the existing planning request. `journal_recoverable` does not assert persistent-media directory synchronization: a power/system failure may lose namespace entries, including retained images or intent. Process-interruption recovery is supported only when its required retained evidence survives; missing evidence requires explicit resolution and never fabricated rollback. Document this persistence limit and report its reduced tier without disabling the platform solely for lack of a stronger namespace flush.
Errors carry code, field and reason strings. Codes are `invalid_request`, `unsupported_schema`, `authority_refused`, `store_not_disjoint`, `barrier_unavailable`, `plan_refused`, `source_changed`, `third_state`, `intent_mismatch`, `journal_invalid`, `journal_io`, `publication_io`, `synchronization_failed`, `preservation_unavailable`, `recovery_ambiguous`. Warnings carry code and action; codes are `observed_conflict`, `publication_uncertain`, `durability_reduced`, `durability_unconfirmed`, `residue_retained`, `metadata_scope_reduced`. Actions are `inspect`, `retry`, `manual_resolution`, `supply_input`. External-writer risk is always expressed in guarantees and documentation; an unobserved race is not invented as an observed conflict. Strict generated readers own structural shape; the operation owner validates schema/protocol values, canonical decimal strings, identities, paths, phase and actual result invariants before any write or emission. Generated reports retain typed effects even on refusal; an error never implies that earlier store or target writes did not occur.

MANIFEST-MIGRATION-SURFACES.title: Explicit CLI and context-bound MCP application

p.MIGRATION-SURFACE-LAW:
**Shared operation, explicit admission.** CLI `vibe refactor migration-operation` and MCP tool `manifest_migration_operation` consume the registered operation request and return the same registered operation report. The request discriminator owns apply, inspect and recover; surfaces do not implement another recipe, journal or report codec. Planning remains the existing separate pure operation.
The CLI consumes stdin or an explicit `--request-json` literal. It runs before configuration promotion, tracing, Context, VVM, registry and progress initialization, as the pure planning entry does. A small shared early-dispatch helper may carry only these two machine entries; unrelated commands retain their existing route. Decode structural shape/schema before opening any project or recovery store. An explicit CLI operation admits its one owned authored-file request, subject to the existing exclusions and physical capability checks; a version or a path spelling alone never grants it. The handler renders exactly one generated report plus newline, retaining all effects, warnings and residue. Completed/no-op exit 0; pending exit 2; uncertain/refused exit 1, except invalid request/schema preflight exits 2. Unreadable stdin is a preflight `invalid_request` with field `request.input`, fixed reason and exit 1; no new wire error code or PlanError response is added. Output failure has exit 1 and a fixed diagnostic; it cannot assert that an operation already performed had no effects.
MCP migration authority is configured by the trusted server composition root, not tool arguments. Add an explicit ServerContext builder for one absolute recovery-store root and a finite portable-relative authored-file allowlist. Compatibility contexts without that builder refuse migration admission before runtime; other tools retain their behavior. The builder creates no filesystem state. It requires an explicit absolute server project root; relative legacy contexts do not acquire a migration grant by guessing cwd. The CLI server composer already resolves its `--path` and may grant migration authority via `vibe mcp serve --migration-recovery-store <absolute-path>` and repeatable `--migration-file <relative-path>`. If a store is supplied with no file flags, only root `vibe.toml` is admitted. File flags without a store are invalid server configuration. This is a bounded grant, not a new authentication framework or a per-operation confirmation flow.
The tool binds the request's project spelling, target operand and store spelling to the configured authority. It opens the trusted project through the existing grant owner, never an arbitrary payload root. A member file is admitted only when explicitly listed; file paths cannot escape or follow links. The recovery store stays physically disjoint from the project and cannot intersect the server's machine package-cache root. Reject lexical ancestor/descendant overlap through the existing path owner; when that cache exists, use the existing-only no-follow disjointness owner to reject physical aliases before recovery-store creation. A missing cache is not initialized. An unbound/relative machine-cache root cannot grant migration authority. Neither tool arguments nor an implicit HOME/default store may override these selections. Normal Linux, macOS and Windows operation remains usable through this explicit configuration and the declared weaker portable contract.
Before runtime entry, strict decode, unsupported schema and admission refusal use the existing generic structured ToolError preflight channel with the owning generated report. After runtime entry, completed/no-op and truthful pending inspection use normal executed ToolOutput; refused/uncertain operation failures retain their full structured effects through executed_failure. No tool-name branch belongs in the dispatcher. Context admission does not load a lockfile, provider, configuration or hosted lifecycle installation. Internal report-validation failure retains its original evidence and cannot be converted to an empty preflight, unchecked normal report or fabricated success. The exactly-one-generated-report rule applies to validated normal results. On this internal invariant failure only, CLI emits no normal-report stdout, exits 1 and writes a labelled diagnostic to stderr containing the validation fault and original evidence. MCP returns an executed diagnostic-only failure with isError true and text containing that same labelled evidence, without normal-report structuredContent. Diagnostic serialization of the retained report is explicitly unvalidated and is never a replay authority. The generic tool seam owns this text-only executed-failure distinction; existing structured results, including a deliberate JSON null, retain their old rendering. No tool-name special case or new domain-error codec is added. Verify this branch with a deliberately inconsistent retained report without performing a new target mutation or claiming it is a normal runtime result.
Verify real isolated CLI startup and MemoryTransport dispatch for all three operations, stdin/literal parity, poisoned configuration and stale VVM, strict/null/unknown input, absent-store inspection without creation, context/file/store refusal, frozen/link/escape cases, exact replay, source conflict and retained interrupted effects. Implementations, Linux native measurements and unperformed macOS/Windows proof remain distinct claims. No surface initializes a user's actual project/store during its test proof, and no public publication is inferred.

our-formats.title: 6. The formats of this project, by name

p.FMT-CATALOG: **6.1 The catalog is three things with three fates.** The read-for-rewrite core (`by-name/`, `repomd.json`) stops being read at all — server mutations become journal appends, `add`/`remove`/`reindex` become reprojections; after that, reader strictness drops for free, `generated_at` comes from the journal (event time, not process clocks), the catalog becomes deterministic and rebuild-testable. The export files (`primary.jsonl(.gz)`, `by-cap/`, `by-purl/`) are strict canonical exports, and every published format must have a *generated reader used in a round-trip test* — publishing what we cannot read back is how write-only formats drift. The narrow public gate — name, version, hash+recipe, URL, yanked, tombstone — is a new, small, slow-moving artifact: the one surface we actually defend before foreign tools, so that everything richer behind it may churn weekly. The catalog repository itself is *declared disposable*: pin content by hash, not by commit — a permission we can actually keep, instead of a promise we cannot.

p.FMT-CATALOG-VERSION: **The catalog's version stops being a number nobody compares.** Its heavy role moves into the *path* (the epoch); its light role into per-record must-understand. The old question "is the version a gate or a declaration?" dissolved because it sought both answers inside one `u32`.

p.FMT-MANIFEST: **6.2 `vibe.toml` is the most expensive format in the system** — authored, unrecoverable, resident in foreign repositories, and an external surface *de facto* because agents read files, not APIs. It is the one place we honestly pay the stability tax: an **epoch marker in the file, introduced before first publication** (absence ≠ "assume 1"; absence is the distinct pre-epoch state, interpreted through an explicitly selected frozen profile; missing profile selection requires input rather than a heuristic); strictness with did-you-mean hints in our namespace (in a hand-written file an unknown key is a typo and the author is present — the asymmetry with the machine-written catalog is principled, not inconsistent); a named reserve section we never touch; a **generated projection as the published copy**, so foreign tools read a recoverable artifact while the hand-written original remains our internal concern; migration by codemod + bot PR; and a minimal surface — every new manifest key is a years-long obligation and requires a break note, a codemod, and generated documentation.

p.FMT-LOCKFILE: **6.3 `vibe.lock` is the cheapest format and becomes free by construction.** "Schema version 5, reject on `!=`" is replaced by: the lockfile is valid only for the exact (epoch, generator hash, recipe ids) that built it; any mismatch → silently regenerate; `--frozen` turns that into a loud error for CI. Deterministic by the same rules as the catalog. Consequence for design: since this format's evolution is free, volatile facts belong here — the bottom rung of the ladder.

p.FMT-CONFIGS: **6.4 Configs are preferences, not data — failure is structurally impossible.** `fn load() -> Config` with no `Result`: unknown key → warning; invalid value → default plus warning; the file is rewritten to canonical form opportunistically. Blocking a build over a stale setting is the worst possible trade at ten releases a day. Strict failure belongs where wrong reading corrupts results; graceful degradation where it only changes comfort.

p.FMT-UNINVENTORIED: **6.5 Surfaces nobody inventoried are formats too.** The seven CLI `--json` reports (scripts and agents parse them), MCP tool schemas (literally a contract with foreign agents), skill/subskill files, the journal, the handshake — each is "something a foreign parser reads", each gets a registry entry, a schema, an epoch and a corpus.

obligations.title: 7. Obligations have types; stability is a mechanism

p.OBLIGATION-TYPES: **Three types of obligation, and only two eternal ones.** *Eternal* (both about honesty, not content): we never present a wrong answer as right; we never answer silence for a name that existed. Both are keepable forever because they forbid no change. *Expiring*: epoch support windows — they do not get broken, they *expire on schedule*. *Revocable*: everything else — names, fields, structures, vocabularies, paths. The owner's prediction «любое обязательство однажды нарушим» is satisfied by construction: almost nothing here is vowed.

p.OBLIGATION-PROCEDURE: **An obligation without a written breaking procedure is a hope, not an obligation.** Every obligation ships with its procedure (announce → transform/reproject → publish in parallel → sunset → leave a tombstone) and the procedure is *rehearsed*: the release pipeline replays a cold upgrade from the oldest supported epoch, and a staged sunset is drilled periodically. Early breaking is the same procedure compressed, plus a recorded owner reason — friction is asymmetric by design: extending a sunset is free, shortening one takes an explicit owner act.

p.STABILITY-IS-A-FLAG: **A period of stability is a closed break window plus a published expiry.** The honest move-fast contract with millions of users is not "we won't break you" but **"you always know the date you break, and the fix is one command."** The date travels inside the world it retires; clients warn ahead of it; on the day, the refusal carries the recipe. Heavy breaks batch into trains — parallel publication and support windows are fixed costs per train, not per change.

p.THE-PUBLIC-SWITCH:
**Historical pre-publication ruling (owner, 2026-08-10, near-verbatim):** «я пока ничего не публиковал на большую публику… я хочу, чтобы мы не применяли миграции до тех пор, пока я не скажу, что состоялось первое представление публике… технически этот факт нельзя определить никак — только владелец может сказать, что это произошло». This records the original rationale, not a technical publication detector or a continuing automatic graduation trigger.
Developer Preview 1 at 1.0.0 has users; the historical no-public-users premise does not describe current state. The next owned product/package line is 1.1.0, distinct from that delivered boundary. [PROP-000 ##OWNED-PROTOTYPE-REGIME](PROP-000.xml#OWNED-PROTOTYPE-REGIME) governs: the owner has not declared graduation, and only the owner's explicit prototype-exit declaration activates the applicable major-breaking obligations. A push, publication, tag, version number or user count cannot substitute for it. `public = true` in `formats/EPOCHS.toml` is owner-managed format-window bookkeeping, not automatic graduation or permission to publish. The next line is held local-only by [NEXT-PUBLICATION-HOLD](PROP-000.xml#NEXT-PUBLICATION-HOLD). No format flag, epoch or support calendar is changed by this policy.
Before owner exit, break machinery reports rather than imposing mandatory migrations, bot PRs, parallel worlds or sunset calendars. Regeneration remains an available prototype recipe, not permission to overwrite users' retained data or the delivered Developer Preview 1 boundary. An explicitly requested local typed migration remains allowed under its separately bound authority; this does not assert a migration implementation. After explicit owner exit, applicable migration, support-window and handshake obligations must be bound for major breaks. Early epoch markers, recipe identity, must-understand and yank remain architecture work, not evidence of an inferred public switch.

agents.title: 8. Laws for AI agents — gates, not admonitions

p.AGENT-PROSE-IS-BROKEN: **Governing rule: a policy that exists only in prose is already broken.** Every rule below lives at one of three levels, preferring the highest: L1 — inexpressible in types (the agent physically cannot write it); L2 — inexpressible in the schema language; L3 — refused by CI. An agent's freedom is confined to three directories: schemas, codemods, and application code; everything else is generated and drift-gated.

p.AGENT-GATES: **The gate set.** G1: all wire I/O through `wire::publish/load(FormatId,…)`; unregistered formats untypeable (L1). G2: serde derives forbidden outside `**/generated/**` (L3). G3: regenerate + `git diff --exit-code` (L3). G4: a writer must not accept a wire-parsed type as input (L1). G5: double-build under different clocks/host/locale/paths must be byte-identical; `now()` banned in writer modules (L1+L3). G6: `rebuild --check` — tear down and reproject from a pinned input (L3). G7: schema/format changes demand a break note; golden wire-diff empty or covered (L3). G8: schema changes refused while the break window is closed (L3). G9: a vocabulary exists in exactly one schema; both wire sides, Rust types, docs and prose lists are generated from it (L1+L3). G10: every derived value carries a recipe id; every recipe has a frozen golden (L3). G11: every published format has a generated reader exercised in round-trip tests (L3). G12: clients must read the corpora of supported epochs; on sunset the same test flips to asserting the refusal text and recipe (L3). G13: schema/format edits never share a commit with application code (L3). G14: config load returns no `Result` (L1). G15: manifest codemods edit the TOML document in place; serialising from a struct is refused (L3).

p.AGENT-MESSAGES: **A gate's message is the only documentation that is reliably read.** Every failure states what was violated, why the rule exists (one sentence), and the exact next command — generated from the registry and break notes, never hand-written. And the agent is left no decisions it gets wrong: strict-or-tolerant, optional-or-required, open-or-closed, field-or-epoch each have exactly one machine answer — policy from the generator, placement from the ladder, epoch from the wire-diff. The agent brings *intent*; the schema fixes form; the generator fixes policy.

p.WIRE-DECISION-PATH: **8a. The wire-work decision path — what an agent does when its task touches a format, in order, no steps skipped:** (1) *Name the format.* Find it in `formats/REGISTRY.toml`; absent → this task mints a format, which is an owner-visible act — stop and surface. (2) *Place the fact.* Walk the ladder (§5) from the bottom: does the lockfile bear it? the exports? only then higher — and a new `vibe.toml` key is a years-long obligation demanding its own break note. (3) *Edit the schema, never the type.* The change is made in `schemas/<format>/e<N>/…`; collections carry an explicit empty-policy annotation; vocabularies live here and nowhere else. (4) *Regenerate* (`cargo xtask codegen`) and write behaviour only against generated types. (5) *Run the wire-diff.* Empty → done. Non-empty → write the break note (what · who fixes · recipe), and let the diff class decide: additive under must-understand → light break, no epoch; shape or meaning of existing data → epoch question, which is an owner fork. (6) *Never touch* `generated/**` by hand, vendored copies, or another epoch's frozen schema — those three edits are always wrong regardless of intent.

p.RISK-RECOVERABILITY: **The recoverability bet.** Upstream sources vanish — deleted repositories, force-pushes, privatisation. If rebuild-from-truth stops being possible and a content-addressed source archive is not built, the index silently becomes authoritative and the whole system degrades into a compatibility regime without its detector. *Trigger:* first observed unreachable source that the journal references → the archive subsystem becomes a mandate, not an idea. This is the likeliest way this document is wrong.

p.RISK-RMW-VOLUME: **The journal/projection rework is a real rebuild, not an edit.** Its cost gate is measured before commitment (the TZ's phase 0 measures the three server mutation paths); if it exceeds the budget, the documented fallback is temporary unknown-capture on the three read-modify-write types — named here explicitly as the compromise it is, so it cannot masquerade as the design.

p.RISK-RAW-PARSERS: **Foreign `curl | jq` will happen regardless of generated clients**, and there will never be a signal of it (raw files in git give no telemetry, by design). The honest posture: assume raw parsing exists, keep the narrow gate genuinely boring, and treat any change to it at the highest severity class.

p.RISK-OVERENGINEERING: **The degenerate-first guard.** The epoch machinery must exist, but its first implementation may be degenerate — one live world and `min_client` in the handshake; parallel publication is built when the second world is actually minted. A gate heavier than the system it guards gets walked around, and a walked-around gate is worse than none: it manufactures false confidence. *Trigger for scaling up:* the first real epoch train, and no earlier.

p.RISK-SECURITY-PARKED: **Signature and authenticity remain parked by the owner's standing ruling (`BACKLOG.md` B-015): mechanism slots only, no cryptography.** What this document adds is ordering, not scope: the must-understand set and the signature *slot* exist in the schema before any tolerance ships, because a tolerant reader that can silently ignore a future signature field is a downgrade attack waiting; slots are irreversible-window work, cryptography is not.

p.SOURCES: **This contract's lore and evidence, so a cold reader entering from either side finds the other:** the architectural reasoning with rejected alternatives is [`vibevm/vibespecs/design/change-native-formats-verdict.xml`](../design/change-native-formats-verdict.xml) (the convened-council verdict, recorded near-verbatim); the research it stands on — ten data-at-rest ecosystems, eight serialization formats, the client-survival study, the wire census of this tree, four adversarial worker reviews and the reviewer's verdict — is imported whole at [`vibevm/vibespecs/research/schema-evolution-2026-08/`](../research/schema-evolution-2026-08/) (reading order: its `12-HANDOFF.xml §2`); the first build that implemented this contract left its reasoning at the anchors of [PROP-005](../modules/vibe-index/PROP-005-package-index.xml) and in the docblocks its phases wrote, never in the plan that carried it. Where lore and this contract disagree, this contract wins and the lore is corrected.

section.title: Opt-in feature migration profiles and transport

p.M05B3-SELECTED-READER: The feature profiles, recipes and exact authored TOML spelling are declared by PROP-003#M05B3-PROFILES through #M05B3-PRESERVATION. These are additional finite edges, not widened materialization or boot-source grammars. The existing plan identities and ordered-edit law apply unchanged. For these edges the current output owner is the actual selected profile-aware core reader, composed from B1 declarations/effects and B2 constraints/selections. Workspace approved-request replay, frozen-coordinate admission and post-publication/recovery checking use that same selected reader. The ordinary Manifest reader remains unchanged.

p.M05B3-QUESTION-WIRE: Feature planning is explicitly selected through migration planning epoch 2 under schemas/migration/e2. Published epoch-1 schemas, readers and question semantics remain unchanged. Epoch 2 retains exact source text and selected source/target/recipe coordinates and adds feature-reference questions with an authored reference identity and finite named corrective choices, distinct from source media/resource paths. Missing interpretation returns needs_input without an application plan; it is not disguised as refused. No answer transport is promised. The existing single-file operation and journal carry the exact approved planning request JSON; their storage, authority, identity and participating-writer guarantees are unchanged.
